workTodo.title: Work todo
workTodo.remindHint: Once per day at the set time, if any open tasks remain (including backlog), you get a notification and this page opens.

tianjiApi.hint: Tianji OpenAI-compatible endpoint: exposes Tianji (tools / approvals / sessions included) as /v1/chat/completions for any OpenAI-compatible client. Setup: base_url is the address below, api_key is the key set here, model is tianji.
tianjiApi.baseUrlHint: base_url: {{baseUrl}}　model: {{model}} (localhost only; use a tunnel for external access. Base URL ends at /v1 — do not append /chat/completions)

aiHub.title: AI Hub
aiHub.shortcutHint: e.g. Ctrl+Alt+K. Change if it conflicts.
aiHub.suggest: Predict the next prompt after every answer
aiHub.suggestHint: The prediction costs one extra model call (counted in the usage table below). Turning it off only removes the chip; Q&A is unchanged.
aiHub.bubbleHint: The panda girl in the corner: pat head / belly / skirt for play only, hold for a hug, double-click opens AI Hub, drag to snap; the right-click menu swaps the skin and opens settings. It mirrors the agent — trots while commands run, nudges you on approval, petals when a round lands; affinity grows as you pet it. Shortcut and tray still open the hub too.
aiHub.petImportEmpty: No custom art yet — import some to unlock this skin.
aiHub.petImportNeedIdle: Assign at least one frame to “Idle”, or the pet has nothing to play.
aiHub.petImportHint: Pick several images, or one n×n sheet: this machine keys out the background, trims each pose and normalises them onto one baseline — nothing leaves your computer.
aiHub.petLicenseHint: Only import art you may redistribute. Most eye-catching open-source pet packs are marked “no commercial use / attribution / share-alike” — keep them out of the installer.
aiHub.petSizeHint: Edge length of the pet window. Switching only affects that window; it re-snaps by its bottom edge and does not jump.
aiHub.petQuietHint: No speech bubbles and no confetti — moods show only through motion. It still knocks when a step waits for you.
aiHub.petResetHint: Affinity returns to 20 and the pet goes back to the bottom-right of the primary screen. Both only affect this pet.
aiHub.diffConfirm: Show the diff before the agent writes
aiHub.diffConfirmHint: At edit level, a file change asks you first (with the diff). Denying leaves the file untouched.
aiHub.rememberedEmpty: Nothing remembered yet — approve a step with「Always allow」and it lands here.
aiHub.webAllowHint: One per line or comma separated; subdomains are included (example.com also allows api.example.com). Empty under the allowlist tier = no fetch. https only, private hosts blocked, every fetch asks first.
aiHub.webTierHint: Off = no web tools. Allowlist = only listed hosts. Open = any public https (private hosts still blocked); every fetch still asks.
aiHub.webSearchHint: web_search is only offered when a provider and key are set. The key stays on this machine.
aiHub.mcpEmpty: None yet. One row is enough: a name (goes into tool names), a command, and its arguments.
aiHub.mcpAdded: Added {{name}}; it applies from the next question
aiHub.mcpHint: Each question starts every enabled server once to list its tools (npx cold start takes a second or two); tools are named mcp_fs_read_file, and each call starts a fresh process that is closed right after. A server decides what its tools can do, so below full access every call asks you first. A server that fails to start only costs this round a few tools; the question still works.
aiHub.subagentsHint: Lets the model hand a wide search to a read-only sub-agent: up to 16 rounds, only 800 characters of findings come back, so the main conversation does not fill with raw matches. It cannot edit files, ask you anything, or spawn another sub-agent. Costs more than a single search.
aiHub.subagentWrite: Let sub-agents edit files / run commands
aiHub.subagentWriteHint: Requires "Allow read-only sub-agents". When on, a sub-agent can also use write / edit / run_command / delete (to Recycle Bin) / move, but only at Edit permission or above (Read / Review never get it). Every write or command reuses the main turn's safety: conflicted repos are refused, protected paths are blocked, Edit shows an approval card first, and undo is shared with the main turn. It still cannot spawn another sub-agent.
aiHub.rememberedScope: Remembered at the narrowest known scope: with a repo selected it is stored per repo + current branch, so switching branch or repo asks once more; only a repo-less session stores it globally. With several service repos selected there is no single branch, so it is stored for the whole workspace.
aiHub.taskModeHint: Auto by default: no tool narrowing. Pin a scene temporarily with /mode in the composer; a dismissible chip shows above the input while pinned.
aiHub.profileHint: A profile only adds a tone/technical hint to the system prompt and may override temperature; what the AI may do is still decided by the permission level.
aiHub.harnessSources: Project: {{project}} · Global: {{global}} (`.ai-workbench/` holds context.md, memory.md, skills/*.md, hooks.json)
aiHub.harnessHint: Pick a repo first; without `.ai-workbench/` the global config in app data is used.
aiHub.planFirstHint: Enables a real plan gate: read-only exploration and update_plan first, then exit_plan_mode waits for your approval before write/command tools unlock. One-line questions are unaffected.
aiHub.parallelReadsHint: Read-only work (reading files, searching, listing folders, locating symbols) may run up to 4 at a time, which shortens the wait. Turn it off to run them strictly one by one: slower, but the steps appear in exactly the order the model asked for them.
aiHub.retriesHint: Automatically backs off and retries up to 3 times when the provider returns 429 (rate limit) or 5xx. Turn it off to fail immediately — useful when the provider bills duplicate requests or you want the real error right away.
aiHub.grepIgnoreHint: Search and find-files skip whatever .gitignore excludes (node_modules, build output). Turn it off to search those folders too — handy for generated code, slower and noisier.
aiHub.contextTokensHint: How many tokens each round may carry (48k by default). Past that it trims in three stages: tool results, then the oldest rounds, then the system prompt. Larger remembers more, but every request costs more and takes longer.
aiHub.resultCapHint: Upper bound for one tool result fed back to the model (12k characters by default); the head and tail are kept, with a hint on how to read on. Smaller saves tokens but cuts long logs and big files into smaller pieces.
aiHub.anthropicStreamHint: On by default: the answer appears word by word. Some relay gateways break SSE mid-stream; turn it off to send a plain request instead — the answer then shows up only once it is complete.
aiHub.mcpEnabledHint: Master switch. When off, this round starts no server processes and offers no mcp_* tools — the whole table below is paused; each server's own toggle still applies.
aiHub.freshContextHint: On by default: questions asked within two minutes reuse the last git snapshot, after a fingerprint check that nothing changed. Turn it off to re-collect every time — always the latest state, at the cost of a short wait per question.

usage.title: AI usage overview
usage.hint: Calls and estimated tokens from AI Hub / reports / commits — stored locally, never uploaded.
usage.todayOver: Today {{used}} / {{cap}} tokens — over budget ({{pct}}%, {{calls}} calls). This only warns; questions are not blocked.
usage.trendBudget: Dashed line = daily budget; bars over it turn red
usage.emptyTrend: No usage in the last 14 days.

data.importWarn: Import will overwrite all local data. This cannot be undone.

about.title: About
about.clearSkipHint: After clearing, v{{version}} will be offered again
about.skippedCleared: Un-skipped v{{version}} — it will be offered again on next start
about.privacyNote: API keys are stored in local SQLite only — do not share the database file

wecom.title: WeCom bot
wecom.groupDiagHint: Check here when it won't connect or answers look wrong
wecom.answerModeHintShort: Auto: pick by intent; Linked prefetches docs/code/logs together.
wecom.answerModeHint: Auto (recommended): classify the question first — for a live-issue investigation it detects the service name / error signature / time window / traceId and uses them to query SkyWalking logs and traces + code to find the root cause, without reading docs first; for 'read the source' it reads code directly; other how/why questions are docs-first, code when needed. It avoids misfires (e.g. 'how is the logging module implemented' is not treated as troubleshooting, '500 lines of code' is not an HTTP error). You can also pin: Docs first (docs only), Docs+code, or Read code. Pinned modes still temporarily allow reading code when the user says 'read the code'.
wecom.docDirHint: Doc folder for Q&A. Doc auto-update keeps its own copy on the Reverse Engineering page; the two don't affect each other.
wecom.skywalkingEnvHint: Test and production each keep their own address, headers, and time zone. Switching applies immediately; troubleshooting uses only the active environment.
wecom.skywalkingTimezoneHint: Select the time zone OAP uses to interpret query times; unset follows this computer. UTC offsets are fixed and do not automatically adjust for daylight saving time.
wecom.skywalkingHintShort: Provide explicit start/end times and keywords; follow traces to query related-service logs, with coverage limits.
wecom.skywalkingHint: SkyWalking OAP address (GraphQL at {addr}/graphql); empty disables the troubleshooting tool. Provide explicit start/end times, keywords, a service name or traceId to query logs and traces, fetch related-service logs, then check the code. DSH checks the log source first, then collects evidence and checks the code. Code-informed log follow-ups are limited to 2 rounds sharing a default 120-second budget and at most 24 HTTP requests. If the source fails or no query is formed, the reply explains why without claiming logs were queried. When the budget is exhausted, it returns collected evidence marked as partial coverage, not a complete search of every service or log, nor unrestricted multi-turn tool use. For authenticated OAP, put Key: Value in Header (e.g. Authorization: Bearer xxx).
wecom.webhookPlaceholder: WeCom group-bot webhook URL or key
wecom.webhookHintShort: Push change notices to WeCom; Feishu/DingTalk optional.
wecom.webhookHint: WeCom group-bot webhook URL (or just the key). After each update, a summary is sent to every configured channel. Stored encrypted; leave blank to keep.
wecom.webhookFeishuPlaceholder: Full https URL of Feishu custom bot
wecom.webhookDingtalkPlaceholder: Full https URL of DingTalk custom bot
wecom.docgenCronHint: A 5-field unix cron (min hour dom mon dow) overrides the daily time above. Every matching minute triggers once (never twice in the same minute), so it can run multiple times per day; leave empty to keep HH:MM. Parse failure skips the tick.
wecom.docgenLookbackDaysHintShort: Only applies to newly added repos or a gap longer than N days; normal runs start from the last cursor.
wecom.docgenLookbackDaysHint: Daily runs never use this: the range always starts at the last collected commit. It only cuts the range in two cases — a repo added to the list with no cursor yet, or a gap longer than N days. In both, the start moves to "N days ago" and anything older is skipped (the cursor then jumps to HEAD). "No limit" replays everything since the last cursor, which can be a lot of history. Max 30 days.
wecom.docgenRepoPathHint: Workspace used only by doc auto-update (the Git repo that holds the docs). It is independent of the workspace in Answer settings — each side runs against its own repos. Leave empty to follow Answer settings. Switching to another repo drops allowlisted sub-repos that no longer live under it.
wecom.docgenDocDirHint: Doc folder used only by doc auto-update (path inside the workspace above, default doc). It is independent of the doc directory in Answer settings; leave empty to follow Answer settings.
wecom.docgenRepoAllowlistHint: Pick Git child repos under the workspace above to watch for changes. Docs still write to the single Document directory. Empty = only the doc-dir repo.
wecom.docgenRepoEmpty: No scan yet, or no child repos under the parent folder.
wecom.docgenRepoRootMissing: Set the workspace path before scanning child repositories.
wecom.docgenRunNeedWorkspace: No workspace configured yet — set it on the Content tab to enable runs.
wecom.docgenSystemPromptHint: Editable system template. Placeholders: {doc_dir} {branch} {commits} {files} {diff}. Empty = built-in default; git still injects the delta; reverse-engineering steps live in your prompt.
wecom.docgenQualityPromptHint: Quality-check system template. Placeholders: {doc_dir} {branch} {files} {summary}. Empty = built-in default.
wecom.docgenPreview: Preview mode (write to disk for review)
wecom.docgenPreviewHint: After the AI run, doc changes stay in the workspace (no commit/push) and a preview notice is sent to the group. Commit manually after review, or discard. Scheduled runs skip while the tree is dirty.
wecom.docgenQualityCheckHint: When on, run a read-only review with the quality prompt after the update (findings go to the notice and history). When off, skip that round — the template stays editable.
wecom.docgenPollReleaseHint: On each minute tick, compare each repository's local HEAD to the last cursor; run once when local HEAD advances and the docs repository is clean (no git hooks; source repositories are not switched or pulled).
wecom.docgenEngineInheritHint: Doc updates reuse the engine picked in Answer settings (currently {{engine}}). Override here to run them on a different engine.
wecom.docgenEngineDshHint: Doc updates run on the local DSH: a separate process in edit tier, stopped right after the run. The Q&A engine and tier are unaffected. DSH must be installed on the Harness page first.
wecom.docgenDshModelHint: Empty means reuse the DSH model and effort from Answer settings; picking one only affects doc updates. Models, keys and sign-in all come from DSH itself — not the model hub.
wecom.docgenDshModelNeedReady: Hit Refresh models to load DSH's model list (it starts a DSH process for a moment and stops it right after).
wecom.docgenEngineTianjiHint: Doc updates use this app's models (Model hub → scene model aiHub) at workspace permission and don't need DSH.
wecom.docgenSyncSourcesHintShort: Fetch and fast-forward source repos first so stale local code is not collected; dirty or diverged repos are skipped.
wecom.docgenSyncSourcesHint: Off by default: only each source repo's local HEAD is read, so commits pushed by others need your own git pull. When on, it runs git fetch origin <release branch> on the allowlisted repos and does a --ff-only fast-forward only when the repo is clean and the local HEAD is an ancestor of the remote branch. Dirty repos, local-ahead or diverged histories, fetch/ff failures are reported and skipped — never rebase, reset or force-push. The docs repo itself is always fetched and fast-forwarded regardless of this switch.
wecom.docgenResetCursorConfirm: Reset the cursors of these {{count}} repos? The next run re-collects their changes from the last {{days}} days (docs already updated may be rewritten).
wecom.docgenResetCursorConfirmAll: Reset the cursors of all repos? The next run re-collects each repo's changes from the last {{days}} days (docs already updated may be rewritten).

docgenPhase.workspace: Checking the workspace and docs directory
docgenPhase.branch: Switching and fast-forwarding the release branch
docgenPhase.agent: AI is updating the reverse-engineering docs

wecom.autoUpdateHintShort: Schedule/cron/poll release, update docs by changes, multi-channel notify.
wecom.autoUpdateHint: On schedule or poll: pull latest release → update reverse docs from commit/diff → notify configured WeCom/Feishu/DingTalk webhooks. Skips on dirty tree; no-op when there is no code change.
wecom.docgenChecklist: Before enabling: (1) the update workspace on the Content tab points at the repo holding the docs (empty = follow Answer settings) (2) release branch name is correct (3) at least one webhook (4) keep Auto-commit on unless Preview (5) run Test, then Update now.
wecom.autoCommitHintShort: git commit the docs so the next run isn't skipped as dirty.
wecom.autoCommitHint: After updating, commit only the doc-folder changes (message auto-generated). If off, the update stays uncommitted and the next auto-update is skipped as 'workspace has uncommitted changes' — unless you commit manually. Keep it on.
wecom.autoPushHint: git push to the release branch after commit (needs push credentials configured). Off by default (local commit only).
wecom.docgenRunNowHint: 'Test' checks release / webhooks / SkyWalking; 'Update now' runs the full flow (pull → edit docs → commit or preview discard → notify).
wecom.hint: Connect via WeCom intelligent-bot long connection (Bot ID + Secret). Outbound only — no public callback URL. DM defaults to pairing; groups default to allowlist. WeCom usually only delivers group messages that @ the bot.
wecom.hintShort: Setup: WeCom intelligent-bot long connection, outbound only
wecom.qrBindHint: Scan with WeCom to create and authorize an intelligent bot; Bot ID / Secret fill in automatically.
wecom.qrSvgMissing: Could not render a local QR SVG. Open the QR page in a browser instead.
wecom.qrScanning: Scan this QR code with WeCom
wecom.corpHint: Business APIs (docs / calendar / smartsheet) require a self-built app's Corp ID + Secret (WeCom admin → Application Management). The bot Bot ID/Secret is only for the message channel and cannot call business APIs.
wecom.corpHintShort: Only needed for docs / calendar / smartsheet; can be left blank.
wecom.selfIntroPlaceholder:
Leave blank for the built-in default. Example: Hi! I'm the AI Workbench Tianji assistant.
Ask me about product/docs, code, or online log troubleshooting…
wecom.selfIntroHint: Used as the WeCom enter-chat welcome and when a message is exactly a greeting or identity prompt ("hello / who are you / what can you do / 你好 / 介绍一下" ...): replied verbatim, no model. "新对话，你好" resets the conversation first, then uses this intro. Longer sentences still go through normal Q&A. Blank uses the default intro.
wecom.selfIntroHintShort: Welcome text on chat open; matched greetings are answered verbatim, no model.
wecom.enhanceEnabledHint: When on, engine Q&A turns append this side's text after the capability card, plus an automatic <wecom_im_source> block (real callback fields only). Self-intro short-circuit is unchanged.
wecom.enhanceDmPlaceholder: Tell the engine how to speak and use context in DMs. You may reference fields inside <wecom_im_source>.
wecom.enhanceGroupPlaceholder: Tell the engine how to speak in groups: keep it short, less spam; rely only on fields already in <wecom_im_source>; do not invent members or chat history.
wecom.enhanceDmSample: In DMs, be conversational and offer one extra suggestion when helpful. Use only the user's words and fields already in <wecom_im_source> (channel / conversationType / senderId / msgid); never invent missing identity or history. Ask before guessing.
wecom.enhanceGroupSample: In groups, keep replies short—lead with the answer, avoid flooding. Use only the @ message and fields already in <wecom_im_source> (including chatId); do not invent other members' words or missing context. Ask one clarifying question instead of long preamble.
wecom.enhanceHint: Only affects engine Q&A (DSH / Tianji); off or empty means no inject.
wecom.maxJobsHintShort: Combined active-turn cap across DMs and groups, default 2.
wecom.maxJobsHint: Active turns across DMs and groups: any integer from 1–32, default 2. Existing valid values such as 3 or 6 are preserved. Each session is serial; messages waiting for its previous turn are counted separately. This is not HTTP concurrency: SkyWalking allows at most 2 in-flight requests per OAP. Higher limits use more local and model quota.
wecom.sessionRulesShort: DMs are isolated by bot + user; groups default to bot + chat + user.
wecom.sessionRulesHint: DM session keys use bot + user; ordinary group sessions use bot + chat + user. Each session runs serially; distinct sessions can run within the global active-turn limit (raise to 4–8 when many people @ the bot at once). Exact commands 新会话 / 新对话 reset the current scope (short history, DSH ACP map, investigation cache); 停止 cancels the running turn; 进度 / 还没好吗 queries status. Ordinary follow-ups reuse an active ACP session. Members who explicitly join a shared task share its context within the same bot and group.
wecom.sharedTasksShort: Explicitly create or join a shared task in the same group.
wecom.sharedTasksHint: Send 创建共享任务 NAME (create), 加入任务 CODE (join), 任务状态 (status), or 退出任务 (leave) in the group. Only the creator can send 结束任务 CODE (end). Task metadata is stored in the local database and expires after 24 hours of inactivity, with at most 200 active tasks and 32 members per task. Ending clears task bindings and context; leaving exits only your own shared session.
wecom.sessionCommandsHint: Commands: 新会话 | 停止 | 进度 | 创建共享任务 NAME | 加入任务 CODE | 任务状态 | 退出任务 | 结束任务 CODE. All in-group replies are visible to members.
wecom.groupVisibilityShort: Group replies are visible to all
wecom.groupVisibilityHint: All group replies, including personal-session replies, shared-task replies and approval prompts, are visible to group members. Local history isolation does not make group messages private.
wecom.sessionMigrationHint: Old group history is not automatically copied to personal or shared tasks; new sessions start with empty context. Old DM records without a known bot identity are not automatically migrated either.
wecom.connectChecklistShort: If it won't connect, check in order
wecom.connectChecklistHint: If disconnected, check: (1) channel enabled (2) Bot ID/Secret correct (3) only one local instance holds the bot lease (4) status lastError and Diagnostics channel logs.
wecom.pairingRestartHint: Note: pending pairing codes live in memory for 1 hour and are lost on app restart — the user must message again to get a new code.
wecom.engineHint: Tianji uses this app's models and four permission tiers; DeepSeek Harness hands the turn to the local DSH (a resident dsh --profile acp process) and keeps DSH's own model and sign-in. Switching reconnects the channel automatically; DMs and groups share the same engine (doc auto-update follows by default — override it on the Doc auto-update page).
wecom.engineHintShort: Tianji uses this app's models; DSH uses the local DSH models and sign-in. Switching reconnects.
wecom.dshPermNote: On DSH, Review equals Edit — there is no Tianji-style "AI reviews first". Mapping: Read-only → read-only sandbox; Edit / Review → workspace-write; Full → unrestricted and never asks. Approvals become chat codes (allow-once / reject-once only). Tianji-only safety (conflict repos, protected paths, command blocklist, delete-to-recycle-bin) applies to the Tianji engine only.
wecom.dshPermHintShort: On DSH, Review equals Edit (no AI pre-review); approvals are one-shot chat codes.
wecom.dshWorkspaceHint: The DSH engine needs an absolute path (it is also the writable workspace); leave blank to use the current Git workspace.
wecom.dshMirrorNone: Not mirrored yet (syncs automatically once the channel is on)
wecom.dshMirrorHint: The managed acp profile mirrors DSH's web profile: bundle list, node_modules junction and the model-related patch layers. After changing plugins or models in DSH, hit "Re-sync".
wecom.dshMirrorHintShort: Mirrors DSH's web profile into acp; hit Re-sync after changing plugins.
wecom.dshResynced: DSH config re-synced, the engine is restarting
wecom.dshModelsHint: {{count}} models grouped by provider; models, keys and sign-in all come from DSH itself. Model "Auto" picks a credentialed model each turn. Switching effort back to "Provider default" opens a fresh ACP session so a prior high/medium is not retained.
wecom.dshModelsEmpty: No usable model in DSH: configure a model and key on the Harness → Models page, then hit "Refresh models".
wecom.dshModelsOff: Turn the channel on (DSH engine) to load the model list automatically.
wecom.fullConfirm: Full permission can control this PC and may be triggered from WeCom. Continue?
wecom.requireMentionHint: WeCom usually only pushes group messages that @ the bot; this switch only changes welcome/hint copy. Add the group to the allowlist to use it.
wecom.requireMentionHintShort: Only affects welcome/hint copy; allowlist the group first.

diag.title: Diagnostics

requests.title: Request event diagnostics
requests.hint: Reads existing local events only; never runs model, network or connectivity probes. Click Query after editing filters. Empty filters show recent events. Paste a raw performance request ID or the redacted hash ID shown in events; both are valid query inputs.
requests.hintShort: Filter by request ID, phase and status (all exact match) or a time range; local records only
requests.timeHint: Enter times in this computer's time zone; they are sent as RFC3339. Leave either boundary blank for no restriction.
requests.privacyHint: Copy includes only loaded event timestamps, request IDs, phases, statuses, codes and durations, with no arbitrary metadata or business text. Export uses the backend's redacted metadata package and asks for a save location; session bodies are excluded.
requests.idle: No query yet. Enter filters and click Query, or select a request in the session log.
requests.queryError: Diagnostic read failed. Verify that the backend supports these APIs, then query again. Failure is not treated as an empty result.
requests.cursorError: Logs were appended, replaced or removed, or the cursor expired. Click Refresh to restart from the latest records. Rename-only rotation remains valid; the next page is never guessed automatically.
requests.timeError: Enter valid times with From no later than To.
requests.actionError: Copy or export failed. Please retry; saving still uses the system picker.
requests.partial: Partial coverage: scan limits, log rotation or read errors may omit events. No events does not mean this request never ran.
requests.readErrors: Read errors occurred (up to 20 distinct entries counted; {{count}} currently). Available events are retained; missing records do not prove absence.
requests.empty: No matching events within these filters and scanned ranges. Records may not exist yet or may have rotated; partial coverage is not a complete empty result.
requests.metadata: Event metadata (preview limited to 4000 characters; export for the full package)
requests.bounded: This view reached its limit (10 pages / 500 events), or the backend cursor stopped advancing. Narrow the filters and query again; this is not a complete history.
requests.end: End of this page sequence; results cover only the readable ranges of this query.

diag.instanceHint: Backend serving this window. When installed and development builds coexist, verify the PID and build label.
diag.jobsHint: Active turns, effective limit, same-session waiting and active shared tasks come from this backend instance. Missing fields display Not reported, never inferred from settings or HTTP counts. Shared tasks are not running turns.
diag.performanceHint: Snapshots of the latest completed phase and same-request summary, not a live timer. Total is execution time; queue time is separate, unlike the chat footer that includes waiting. Character and tool-event counts are backend observations. Missing fields display Not reported.
diag.performanceHintShort: Snapshot of the latest completed phase and same-request summary; not a live timer
diag.phaseTableHint: Shows only this request's backend summary. The latest phase is not added again; parent phases such as planning and their children are not summed twice. Execution total is timed independently, not calculated from this table. First event is not first token; tool events are not unique tool calls. Model and effort are backend records. A configuration ACK confirms only the selected settings, not observed model usage. Unobserved values do not confirm the actual configuration.
diag.validationFailures: Total validation failures: {{countText}} (bounded samples below; a missing total is not inferred from sample count)
diag.cacheHitsHint: Cache hits belong to the latest investigation and include successful responses reused after singleflight waits, not actual HTTP requests. Compare request IDs with the performance record; they may belong to different turns.
diag.countHint: Collected, shown, collected WARN, truncated and pending-page counts come from this backend instance only; cumulative follow-ups may include duplicates. Missing fields display Not reported, never zero. Zero unexplained decisions only means no gaps were reported, not a verified root cause; a normal trace does not rule out business exceptions. Not executed differs from an empty result; reply text does not prove source access.

investigationState.time_window_mismatch: Returned evidence is outside the time window
investigationState.empty: Query completed with no matching evidence

diag.sessionReadFailed: Session sidecar read failed. Previous results are retained if available; failure is not an empty result. Refresh to retry.
diag.sessionPartial: Partial session sidecar coverage: bounded scans, rotation or read errors may omit records. An empty view does not prove there were no sessions.
diag.sessionReadErrors: Sidecar read errors ({{count}} entries; expand codes)
diag.logHint: Recent send/receive / gate / errors (from wecom.log) — check here when the bot does not reply.
diag.sessionHint: Recent WeCom Q&A sidecar (read-only) for reviewing multi-turn context. Local history isolation does not make group messages private; group replies remain visible to group members.

weixin.pluginHint: On your phone, enable the WeChat bot plugin under Me → Settings → Plugins first.
weixin.pluginHintShort: Enable the WeChat bot plugin on your phone first
weixin.qrRebindHint: Scanning again replaces the current bot credential and bound user.
weixin.empty: No WeChat bot bound yet. Scan the QR code to answer DMs.
weixin.qrBindHint: Scan with WeChat. If a pairing code appears, enter it below.
weixin.qrScanning: Scan this QR code with WeChat
weixin.answerReuseHint: Answer engine, mode, workspace, and doc folder are shared with the WeCom tab.
